summary: Mattia Salvini is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and SOAS University of London (PhD ~2003–2011 under Tadeusz Skorupski), later holding posts at Mahidol University (~2011) and the International Buddhist College.

Mauli Chand Prasad is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral dissertation at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University under B. Jinanand and U. Dharmaratna, and served as Lecturer in Pali at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (attested 1984).

Maurice Bloomfield (1855–1928) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Furman, Yale, and Johns Hopkins (PhD ~1878–1879), under scholars including William Dwight Whitney and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He served as professor at Johns Hopkins University from 1881 to 1926.

Maurice Frank Wiles (1923–2005) was a religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge. He held posts at Ridley Hall, the University of Ibadan, the University of Cambridge, and King's College London, before serving as Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford (1970–1991).

Maurice Grammont (1866–1946) was a linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1888–1892) under Ferdinand de Saussure. He held a post at the University of Montpellier from around 1895 to 1939.
Maurice Jametel (1856–1889) was a scholar in Sinology and Tibetology. He studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes and later held a post there from around 1886 until 1889.

Maurice Leenhardt (1878–1954) was a scholar of religious studies and other fields. He studied under Marcel Mauss, whom he later succeeded, and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from around 1940 to 1953.

Maurice O'Connell Walshe (1911–1998) worked in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He studied under Walpola Rahula and held a post at the Institute of Germanic and Romance Studies from around 1958 to 1979.

Maurine Stuart (1922–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at the University of Manitoba and under teachers including Nadia Boulanger, Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani, Eido Shimano, and Soen Nakagawa. In 1979, she became president and spiritual director of the Cambridge Buddhist Association.

Maurizio Taddei (1936–2000) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as a professor at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and as Director of the Editorial Committee at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East.

Mauro Maggi specializes in Iranian, Central Asian, and Tibetology studies. He completed a doctoral thesis at the University of Naples "L'Orientale", served as Director at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East, and held a post at Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2018).

Mavis L. Fenn specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the Universities of Winnipeg and Calgary, and earned her PhD at McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen, later holding posts at United College and the University of Waterloo.

Max Deeg is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and Sinologist who completed his PhD and Habilitation at the University of Würzburg. He served as Head of School at Cardiff University (attested 2010–2021) and as Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Max Kaltenmark (1910–2002) was a Sinologist and religious studies scholar. He served as director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1949–1953) and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Paris from around 1957 to 1979.

Max Leopold Margolis (1866–1932) was a linguist and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD at Columbia. He held posts at Columbia, Hebrew Union College, the University of California, and Dropsie College for Hebrew and Cognate Learning (1909–1932).
Max Lindenau was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Leipzig until 1913 under Ernst Windisch.

Max Oidtmann (born 1979) specializes in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. Educated at Carleton College, Indiana University, and Harvard under Mark Elliott, he has held academic posts at Georgetown University, Georgetown University in Qatar, and the University of Munich.

Max Scheler (1874–1928) was a philosopher who studied at the universities of Munich, Berlin, and Jena. He held academic posts at the University of Jena (~1900–1907), University of Munich (~1907–1910), University of Göttingen, and University of Cologne (~1919–1928).

Max Walleser (1874–1954) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Erlangen-Nuremberg, founded the Institut für Buddhismus-Kunde Heidelberg in 1928, and served as professor of Indian philology at Heidelberg University (1918–1936).
May Oung (1880–1926) was an active figure in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Cambridge from around 1904 to 1908 and founded the Burma Research Society in 1910.
